title: Senior Officers from BRICS Member Countries hold discussions on Key Priorities of the Environment Working Group and Contact Group on Climate Change and Sustainable Development in New Delhi
body_text:
Under India’s BRICS Chairship 2026, Senior Officers’ Meeting of the Environment Working Group and Contact Group on Climate Change and Sustainable Development was held in Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 17th August 2026. The meeting was chaired by Secretary, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India, Shri Tanmay Kumar. The proceedings witnessed participation from BRICS member countries including Federative Republic of Brazil, People’s Republic of China, Arab Republic of Egypt, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Republic of Indonesia, Islamic Republic of Iran, Russian Federation, Republic of South Africa and United Arab Emirates.
Secretary, @moefcc , Shri Tanmay Kumar, welcomed the distinguished delegates from BRICS Member Countries to the Environment Working Group-Senior Officers' Meeting affirming solidarity & shared commitments towards a sustainable future. #BRICS2026 #BRICSIndia2026 … pic.twitter.com/6T5n3bWabA — MoEF&CC (@moefcc) August 17, 2026
In his keynote address, the Chair stated that over the past two decades, the BRICS alliance has expanded from an economic dialogue into an increasingly influential platform for defining its approach to the critical challenges facing the environment, including pressing global issues of increasing pollution, biodiversity loss as well as global warming. He said, "Our partnership has broadened in terms of relevance to sustainable development, climate resilience and adaptation, resource efficiency and circular economy, as well as  environmental governance."
The Chair informed that BRICS 2026 has been guided by the vision of the Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, that global cooperation must remain people-centric by advancing a humanity-first approach. This vision finds expression in the Chairship theme - 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability'. India has sought to advance environmental action through approaches that integrate ecological sustainability with development objectives, it was stated.
Over the course of India’s Chairship, the Environment Working Group and the Contact Group on Climate Change and Sustainable Development have together advanced cooperation across four interconnected priority areas: Promoting Sustainable Lifestyles; Afforestation, Forest Fire Management and Disaster Resilience; Circular Economy and Adaptation.
The Chair stated that these priorities reflect both the shared environmental challenges confronting the BRICS countries and the collective wisdom and strength to address them. They reflect the unanimous recognition that climate resilience, ecosystem restoration, resource efficiency and sustainable development are deeply interconnected challenges that require integrated and holistic responses rather than isolated interventions in silos.
It was informed that since the commencement of India’s Chairship, Member Countries have engaged through 21 virtual thematic and negotiation meetings, 10 bilateral consultations, 2 thematic dialogues and 2 technical webinars, reflecting an extraordinary level of commitment to advancing the shared agenda. The marathon deliberations would culminate in building a consensus on the key priorities during the Senior Officers' meeting being held today.
Concluding the address, the chair expressed confidence that the spirit of co-operation and mutual respect which has guided the collective dialogues and discussions so far  would continue to guide the deliberations today. The 12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting is scheduled to be held in New Delhi tomorrow.
The participating delegations from the BRICS member countries congratulated India for its successful leadership as the BRICS Chair and bringing together each side through productive deliberations on the priority areas, under an atmosphere of mutual respect, trust and consensus-based decision making.

ministry.name: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

enrichment.summary: On 17 August 2026, India hosted a Senior Officers' Meeting of the BRICS Environment Working Group and Contact Group on Climate Change and Sustainable Development in New Delhi, chaired by MoEFCC Secretary Tanmay Kumar. Delegates from Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, South Africa and UAE discussed four priority areas under India's 2026 BRICS Chairship: sustainable lifestyles, afforestation and forest fire management, circular economy, and climate adaptation. The meeting preceded the 12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting scheduled for the next day in New Delhi.
enrichment.context:
BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, now expanded to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and UAE) has evolved from a purely economic grouping into a platform addressing environmental and climate governance, reflecting the growing weight of emerging economies in global climate negotiations such as UNFCCC COPs. India's 2026 BRICS Chairship theme, 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability,' aligns with India's broader diplomatic push to position itself as a voice for the Global South on climate justice, common but differentiated responsibilities, and sustainable lifestyles (echoing India's LiFE - Lifestyle for Environment initiative launched at COP26/G20).

This Senior Officers' Meeting was a preparatory step ahead of the 12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting, where formal outcomes and joint statements on the four priority areas are expected to be adopted. Such BRICS environmental cooperation mechanisms are significant for India's foreign policy as they allow coordination among major developing economies on issues like climate finance, technology transfer, and adaptation funding, often as a counterweight to developed-country positions in multilateral forums.

prelims_questions.question: Consider the following countries: 1. Egypt 2. Indonesia 3. Iran 4. UAE. Which of the above are members of BRICS as of 2026?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and UAE (along with Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa) are all listed as BRICS member countries participating in the meeting, confirming the expanded BRICS grouping.

prelims_questions.question: India's 2026 BRICS Chairship theme is centered on which of the following concepts?
options: Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability
One Earth, One Family, One Future
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states India's BRICS 2026 Chairship theme is 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability.'

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of BRICS as an emerging platform for environmental and climate governance among developing economies. How does India's 2026 Chairship priorities align with its domestic and international climate commitments?
Examine the four priority areas identified under India's BRICS Environment Working Group Chairship in 2026 and their relevance to sustainable development in emerging economies.

study_notes.reason: The release gives a testable factual core (BRICS composition, India's 2026 Chairship theme, the four priority areas, the 12th Environment Ministers' Meeting) while also offering material on India's climate diplomacy strategy and Global South positioning that can be analytically deployed.

prelims.point: BRICS now comprises 10 members: original Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa plus Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, and UAE
prelims.why_important: UPSC frequently tests grouping membership and recent expansions; the 2024 BRICS expansion is a high-probability factual item.

prelims.point: India held the BRICS Chairship in 2026 with theme 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability'
prelims.why_important: Chairship themes of India-led groupings are recurring factual questions in current affairs-based prelims.

prelims.point: 12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting was held in New Delhi, preceded by a Senior Officers' Meeting of the Environment Working Group and Contact Group on Climate Change and Sustainable Development
prelims.why_important: Sequence and nomenclature of BRICS institutional mechanisms (Working Groups vs Ministerial Meetings) can be tested as factual detail.

prelims.point: Four BRICS 2026 environmental priority areas: Sustainable Lifestyles, Afforestation/Forest Fire Management/Disaster Resilience, Circular Economy, and Adaptation
prelims.why_important: Specific thematic priorities under an India-led forum are the kind of enumerated list UPSC likes to test via 'which of the following' questions.

mains.point: BRICS environmental cooperation reflects India's strategy to position itself as a voice for the Global South on climate justice and common but differentiated responsibilities
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on India's role in shaping multilateral environmental governance or South-South cooperation on climate change.

mains.point: BRICS has evolved from a purely economic grouping into a platform for environmental governance, showing institutional broadening of regional groupings
mains.analytical_use: Can support answers on how economic blocs adapt mandates to address non-traditional/global issues like climate change.

mains.point: Promotion of 'sustainable lifestyles' echoes India's LiFE initiative, linking domestic climate policy to multilateral platforms
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on India's initiatives for behavioural change in climate action and their international projection.

mains.point: Such forums enable coordination among major developing economies on climate finance, technology transfer, and adaptation funding, acting as a counterweight to developed-country positions
mains.analytical_use: Relevant for essay/GS2 questions on equity in climate negotiations and the role of developing-country coalitions in UNFCCC processes.
